supplementary_news.content_title: Health Canada Authorizes Moderna's mRNA Influenza and Combination Influenza and COVID-19 Vaccines
supplementary_news.content: Canada becomes the first country to authorize both Moderna’s mRNA seasonal influenza vaccine, mFLUSIVA ® , and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine, mCOFLU ® CAMBRIDGE, MA / ACCESS Newswire / November 5, 2026 / Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) today announced that Health Canada has authorized mFLUSIVA ® (Influenza mRNA vaccine; mRNA-1010) and mCOFLU ® (Combined Influenza and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine; mRNA-1083) for adults 50 years of age and older. Canada is the first country in the world to authorize both Moderna’s seasonal mRNA influenza vaccine and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine. “Health Canada’s authorizations of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU today mark another important step in bringing the benefits of mRNA technology to seasonal respiratory vaccination. It’s not every day that a company gets two product approvals on the same day,” said Stéphane Bancel, Chief Executive Officer of Moderna. “Influenza and COVID-19 continue to place a significant burden on public health, particularly among older adults. These milestones reflect our commitment to advancing innovative vaccine options that help protect Canadians and support more resilient health systems.” mFLUSIVA is Canada’s first mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, while mCOFLU is the country’s first combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine. Health Canada’s authorizations follow the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s approval of mFLUSIVA in August 2026 and the European Commission’s authorization of the Company’s combination influenza and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, marketed as mCOMBRIAX®, in April 2026. Both vaccines remain under regulatory review in additional markets. mFLUSIVA is authorized for active immunization of adults 50 years of age and older for the prevention of influenza disease caused by influenza virus subtypes A and B represented in the vaccine. i mCOFLU is authorized for active immunization of adults 50 years of age and older for the prevention of influenza disease caused by influenza virus types A and B represented in the vaccine and SARS-CoV-2. ii Health Canada’s authorization of mFLUSIVA is supported by the pivotal Phase 3 mRNA-1010-P304 study (NCT06602024), a randomized, active-controlled trial involving approximately 40,800 adults 50 years of age and older across 11 countries. mFLUSIVA met all pre-specified statistical success criteria, including the highest level of pre-specified superiority, demonstrating relative vaccine efficacy of 26.6% (95% CI: 16.7-35.4) in adults 50 years of age and older and 27.4% (95% CI: 12.1-40.0) in adults 65 years of age and older compared with a standard-dose inactivated influenza vaccine against RT-PCR-confirmed, protocol-defined influenza-like illness caused by influenza A or B. iii The authorization is also supported by the Phase 3 mRNA-1010-P303 Part C study (NCT05827978), which demonstrated superior antibody responses compared with a high-dose inactivated influenza vaccine in adults 65 years of age and older. iv Across both studies, the most commonly reported adverse reactions included injection-site pain, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, joint pain, chills and axillary (underarm) swelling or tenderness. Most solicited reactions were mild to moderate and resolved within one to two days. v mCOFLU builds on the clinical development of mFLUSIVA and mNEXSPIKE ® . Health Canada’s authorization of mCOFLU is supported by a pivotal Phase 3 trial (NCT06097273), a randomized, observer-blind, active-controlled study evaluating safety, reactogenicity and immunogenicity in two cohorts of approximately 4,000 adults each. Adults 65 years of age and older received mCOFLU or co-administered Fluzone HD ® , a high-dose influenza vaccine, and Spikevax ® , Moderna’s licensed COVID-19 vaccine. Adults 50 to 64 years of age received mCOFLU or co-administered Fluarix ® , a standard-dose influenza vaccine, and Spikevax. vi The study met all primary endpoints demonstrating non-inferiority of immune responses. Following a single dose, mCOFLU elicited statistically significantly higher immune responses against three influenza strains (A/H1N1, A/H3N2 and B/Victoria) and SARS-CoV-2 in both age cohorts compared with co-administered licensed comparator vaccines. The exception was B/Yamagata, a strain no longer recommended for inclusion in seasonal influenza vaccines, for which a statistically significantly higher immune response was not observed in adults 65 years of age and older. vii mCOFLU demonstrated an acceptable safety and tolerability profile. The most commonly reported adverse reactions included injection-site pain, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, joint pain, chills and axillary (underarm) swelling or tenderness. Most were mild to moderate and short in duration. No serious adverse events were assessed as related to mCOFLU in the pivotal study. viii Moderna will engage with Canadian health authorities and immunization partners as it advances plans for the future availability of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU in Canada. About Moderna Moderna is a pioneer and leader in the field of mRNA medicine. Through the advancement of its technology platform, Moderna is reimagining how medicines are made to transform how we treat and prevent diseases. Since its founding, Moderna’s mRNA platform has enabled the development of vaccines and therapeutics across infectious diseases, cancer, rare diseases and more. With a global team and a unique culture, driven by the company’s values and mindsets, Moderna’s mission is to deliver the greatest possible impact to people through mRNA medicines. For more information about Moderna, please visit modernatx.com and connect with us on X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and LinkedIn. mFLUSIVA ® , mCOFLU ® , Spikevax ® , mCOMBRIAX ® and mNEXSPIKE ® are registered trademarks of Moderna. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended, including regarding: Moderna’s engagement with Canadian health authorities and immunization partners; the future availability of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU in Canada; the potential of Moderna’s mRNA platform to advance respiratory disease prevention; and the review of additional regulatory applications of Moderna’s influenza and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccines in other markets. The forward-looking statements in this press release are neither promises nor guarantees, and you should not place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements because they involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and other factors, many of which are beyond Moderna’s control and which could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by these forward-looking statements. This week in Other Barks & Bites: The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has sworn in former counsel to Judge Pauline Newman as Solicitor; Reuters reports that this week’s massive tech selloff could delay the anticipated initial public offering of Anthropic stock; the Western District of Washington releases an unredacted version of the Federal Trade Commission’s complaint over Amazon’s covert price shifting for ad auctions; a Government Accountability Office Report shows that backlog reduction efforts at the USPTO are contributing to patent examiner attrition, in turn making agency goals unsustainable; Circuit Judge Kurt Engelhardt argues that a Fifth Circuit majority misconstrued several likelihood of confusion factors in reversing a district court ruling against Casa Azul’s trademark infringement claims; the Second Circuit affirms a $4 million statutory damages award over a luxury good reseller’s sale of counterfeit Chanel goods not found in the company’s internal inventory database; the Federal Circuit hears oral arguments on Moderna’s government-supplier defense in a patent infringement case brought over its COVID-19 vaccine; and the Copyright Office extends the deadline for initial comments responding to its notice of inquiry on music streaming fraud to mid-December. Bites Greg Dolin Sworn in as USPTO Solicitor – Greg Dolin, former attorney with the New Civil Liberties Alliance (NCLA), where he served as counsel to Judge Pauline Newman in her battle against U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit Chief Judge Kimberly Moore, has been sworn in as the new U.S. Patent and Trademark Office Solicitor, according to IPWatchdog sources. The role would mean Dolin is in charge of representing the Office at the CAFC, which he actively challenged on behalf of Newman during his tenure as Senior Litigation Counsel with the NCLA. Following that role, Dolin joined the Department of Justice (DOJ) as Senior Counsel in the Civil Rights Division. He is also a Professor of Law at the University of Baltimore, where he has been on the faculty since 2011. Dolin has also served as clerk to Judge Newman and as Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Palau. GAO Report Says USPTO Backlog Reduction Efforts Creating Unsustainable Examiner Attrition – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) issued a report requested by Representatives Jamie Raskin (D-MD) and Hank Johnson, Jr. (D-GA) into efforts at the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office to reduce the backlog of unexamined U.S. patent applications from the January 2025 high mark of 838,000 patent applications down to a stated goal of 599,000. According to USPTO data and survey feedback, the GAO’s report found that the agency’s backlog reduction goal is unsustainable due to current high levels of attrition among the agency’s patent examiner workforce, which itself is being caused due to workplace strain from increased examiner workloads, the adoption of AI tools that are currently ineffective for prior art searching, reductions in patent examiner training and less flexible remote work policies. CAFC Mulls Moderna’s Government-Supplier Defense on COVID-19 Vaccine Appeal – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit heard oral arguments in COVID-19 vaccine developer Moderna’s appeal from a ruling by the District of Delaware that it was not immune from patent infringement liability over claims asserted by rival vaccine developers Arbutus and Genevant to a share of royalties from the sale of the COVID vaccine Spikevax. Questioning from the Federal Circuit panel, including Circuit Judges Richard Taranto and Jimmie Reyna, focused on Moderna’s defense that its vaccine shots were made for the U.S. federal government and thus the government should stand in as the defendant in the patent infringement proceedings, a position backed by the U.S. government in briefing during the Delaware district court proceedings. Unredacted FTC Complaint Alleges Amazon Covertly Raising Ad Prices By 250% – On Thursday, November 5, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) announced that the agency had recently filed an updated version of a complaint filed in the Western District of Washington against e-commerce giant Amazon along with attorneys general (AGs) or consumer protection divisions from 22 states over Amazon’s alleged use of deceptive and unfair practices to secretly inflate prices for its online search advertising auctions. Among the unredacted allegations are included Amazon’s secret raising of auction prices by 50% on normal auction days up to as much as 250% on major holidays like Black Friday or Prime Day, with some advertisers experiencing average cost-per-click increases of over 200% during the 2021 holiday season. Circuit Judge Engelhardt Dissents From Fifth Circuit Vacatur in Casa Azul Trademark Case – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit issued a ruling in Casa Tradición S.A. de C.V .v. Casa Azul Spirits, L.L.C. in which a panel majority vacated the Southern District of Texas’ judgment that Casa Azul failed to show a likelihood of confusion between its own tequila product and Casa Tradición’s “CLASE AZUL”-branded tequila after the appellate court found clear error in the district court’s analysis of several likelihood of confusion marks, including that “CLASE AZUL” was suggestive rather than descriptive. Writing in partial dissent was Circuit Judge Kurt Engelhardt who would affirm the district court’s finding of no likelihood of confusion, charging the appellate panel majority with misapplying the clear error standard of review and misconstruing several likelihood of confusion factors including strength of the mark, including the district court’s findings of conceptual and commercial weakness that Judge Engelhardt found to be supported by the trial record. Fifth Circuit Affirms Dismissal of IP Claims Due to Valid TTRPG Licensing Agreement – On Wednesday, November 4, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit issued a ruling in Thomas v. Leyline Publishing, L.L.C. affirming a summary judgment ruling by the Northern District of Texas dismissing a lawsuit including trademark and other intellectual property claims filed by tabletop role playing game (TTRPG) developer Shawn Thomas following a disagreement with game publisher Leyline over a licensing agreement to Thomas’ game “Realms of Kymoria.” The Fifth Circuit found that Leyline Publishing did not breach the licensing agreement for failure to pay for certain content before using it, including content for which Thomas had not yet billed Leyline, and that the district court correctly inferred a trademark license from the agreement’s language allowing Leyland to share the content it purchased under its own branding. AG Szpunar Tells CJEU That Google Gemini Chatbots May Infringe Press Rights – On Tuesday, November 3, Advocate General (AG) Maciej Szpunar of the Court of Justice for the European Union (CJEU) issued an opinion in the first generative artificial intelligence (AI) case to reach the CJEU, involving Google Gemini’s of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology to collect information in real-time from Internet sources to improve the reliability and accuracy of AI chatbot answers. Clarifying the circumstances under which such a process could infringe the rights of press publishers under EU law, AG Szpunar urged the CJEU to find that, as limited to answers provided by chatbots and not within the broader context of AI training, the reuse of content from a press publisher’s website may infringe those rights when the chatbot circumvents effective technical measures protecting the content, such as a paywall, or reuses any of the publication’s expression in a recognizable manner. Barks Copyright Office Extends Comment Period on Music Streaming Fraud NOI to December 18 – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Copyright Office announced that the agency was extending the deadline for the submission of public comments in response to its October notice of inquiry (NOI) on streaming music fraud, with initial comments due December 18 and reply comments due January 29, 2027. Copyright Office Hits Milestone of 25,000 Digitized Copyright Historical Record Books – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Copyright Office announced that a total of 25,238 bound copyright historical record books have been digitized for inclusion in the Copyright Historical Record Books Collection, which now contains more than 21.7 million images of copyright applications and other records bound in books dating from 1870 to 1977. Trademark Suit Filed in District of Minnesota Between “JOHNNIES” Collegiate Athletic Programs – On Thursday, November 4, the Collegeville, MN-based school Saint John’s University filed a lawsuit alleging claims of trademark infringement in the District of Minnesota against New York City-based St. John’s University alleging a likelihood of consumer confusion over the use of the “JOHNNIES” trademark, registered by Minnesota’s Saint John’s school and used by both universities to refer to teams within their respective athletic departments. Second Circuit Affirms Willful Counterfeiting Verdict, $4M Statutory Damages for Chanel – On Tuesday, November 3, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit issued a summary order in Chanel, Inc. v. What Goes Around Comes Around LLC affirming an award of $4 million in statutory damages to Chanel for What Goes Around’s use of a counterfeit mark over sales of stolen or otherwise missing Chanel merchandise removed from that company’s ORLI internal inventory system. Tenth Circuit Dismisses Copyright Damages Appeal for Lack of Appellate Jurisdiction – On Tuesday, November 3, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit issued a ruling in The Capture Eleven Group v. Otter Products, LLC dismissing cross-appeals from a jury verdict awarding Capture Eleven $3 million in profit disgorgement and $114,000 in actual damages for copyright infringement after finding the district court’s order granting a stipulated motion for certification under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b) as the order did not clearly articulate reasons and make careful statements regarding finality in light of third-party litigation in the case. Second Circuit Affirms Prison Sentence, Restitution in Criminal Counterfeiting Case – On Tuesday, November 3, the Second Circuit issued a ruling in United States v. Sow affirming the Southern District of New York’s judgment sentencing Adama Sow to 24 months’ imprisonment, three years’ supervised release and more than $111,000 in restitution after pleading guilty to one count of trafficking in counterfeit goods related to trafficking at least $3.1 million in counterfeit luxury goods through a Gotham Mini-Storage facility in Manhattan. This Week on Wall Street Massive Tech Stock Selloff on AI Regulatory Concerns Could Delay Anthropic IPO – On Thursday, November 5, international news agency Reuters reported on comments provided to Reuters from those familiar with discussions between potential investors and AI company Anthropic that this week’s massive tech stock selloff following this year’s midterm elections, leading to concerns in the data center business world over enhanced regulatory scrutiny by Democrats, which could delay Anthropic’s intention to launch an initial public offering (IPO) of company stock at the company’s current $1.5 trillion valuation. Provider News Provider News Seattle Children’s Providing Influenza and COVID-19 Vaccinations to Patients Nov. 4, 2026 As the annual viral surge continues to grow, it’s important to provide easy access for pediatric patients to receive influenza and COVID-19 vaccinations to reduce the spread of illness. Please review the information below about how current Seattle Children’s patients can access vaccinations. Vaccinations given to patients will be documented in the Child Profile Immunization Registry. For questions about influenza and COVID-19 vaccinations at Seattle Children’s, please visit seattlechildrens.org. Influenza Vaccines at Seattle Children’s Influenza vaccines are available to current patients at Seattle Children’s Hospital and subspecialty and regional clinics, including patients in its urgent care locations and the emergency department. Patients will be screened for eligibility. Seattle Children’s will also provide downloadable flu shot vouchers to patients’ family members and household contacts ages 3 years and older during patient visits; the vouchers can be used at any Albertsons-owned pharmacies and stores with no out-of-pocket cost (family members’ insurance will be billed if available, and any remaining balance will be charged to Seattle Children’s). Family members and household contacts from 6 months to 35 months old will need to get their flu vaccine at their primary care provider’s office. COVID-19 Vaccines at Seattle Children’s COVID-19 vaccines are available for patients ages 6 months and older who are currently admitted or on-site for a clinic appointment. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Sunday, November 8, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Twelve-Week Olfactory Training Improves Persistent Post-COVID-19 Smell Loss in Randomized Trial by November 6, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Twelve-Week Olfactory Training Improves Persistent Post-COVID-19 Smell Loss in Randomized Trial Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A twelve-week regimen of structured olfactory training led to significant and clinically meaningful improvements in smell function among adults experiencing persistent olfactory dysfunction after SARS-CoV-2 infection, according to results from a single-centre, randomized, controlled, assessor-blinded trial. The study, designated as the SMELL trial, addressed a condition that is common, prolonged, and disabling following infection, and for which validated therapeutic options have remained limited. Investigators evaluated adult participants aged 18 years and older who had experienced at least three months of ongoing olfactory dysfunction after a documented SARS-CoV-2 infection and who demonstrated measurable baseline impairment on Sniffin’ Sticks identification testing. Because the trial protocol was designed during the COVID-19 pandemic under contemporaneous infection-control recommendations, the researchers implemented specific methodological modifications to ensure participant safety. Olfactory assessments were performed by drawing an odor line onto single-use filter paper strips rather than presenting the reusable Sniffin’ Stick pen directly beneath each participant’s nose. This technique proved feasible for conducting both Sniffin’ Stick identification and Sniffin’ Stick discrimination testing; however, it was not feasible for odor threshold assessment, which was consequently omitted. To account for this adaptation, the study used a prespecified modified Sniffin’ Sticks total score, calculated by combining the identification and discrimination scores, with the primary study endpoint defined as the change in this modified total score from baseline to twelve weeks. Study screening proceeded through October 31, 2024, during which a total of 77 candidates were assessed. From this screened group, 70 participants were randomly assigned either to undergo twelve weeks of olfactory training or to receive no intervention, representing the natural course of recovery. A total of 68 participants completed the randomized phase of the trial and were included in the primary per-protocol analysis, consisting of 38 participants allocated to the active olfactory training intervention and 30 participants allocated to the untreated control group. Discover more Find ENT Doctors Read Med Journals Study Anatomy COVID-19 Get Rapid Tests The trial demonstrated that twelve weeks of olfactory training significantly improved modified Sniffin’ Sticks total scores compared with the control condition, yielding a statistically significant time-by-group interaction of F(1, 66) = 29.95 (p < 0.001; partial η2 = 0.31). Statistically significant interaction effects favouring the intervention were likewise observed across both subcomponents, with identification scores achieving p < 0.001 (partial η2 = 0.27) and discrimination scores achieving p < 0.001 (partial η2 = 0.19). Protocol-defined clinically relevant improvement in the modified total score occurred in 22 of 38 participants (57.9%) in the olfactory training arm compared to 2 of 30 participants (6.7%) in the control group (φ = 0.53, p < 0.001). Furthermore, assessments of global improvement reported by patients and evaluated by clinicians independently favoured the olfactory training group. Predefined subgroup evaluations confirmed consistent treatment benefits among individuals whose olfactory loss had persisted for more than 6 months as well as those with ongoing loss exceeding 12 months. In addition, participants initially assigned to the control group who subsequently received training during an exploratory extension phase demonstrated significant gains in total modified scores, identification scores, and discrimination scores. No serious adverse events occurred throughout the trial, leading the study team to conclude that structured olfactory training offers a safe, practical, and scalable treatment option for persistent post-COVID-19 smell dysfunction. supplementary_news.content_title: Health Canada Authorizes Moderna's mRNA Influenza and Combination Influenza and COVID-19 Vaccines
supplementary_news.content: Canada becomes the first country to authorize both Moderna’s mRNA seasonal influenza vaccine, mFLUSIVA ® , and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine, mCOFLU ® CAMBRIDGE, MA / ACCESS Newswire / November 5, 2026 / Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) today announced that Health Canada has authorized mFLUSIVA ® (Influenza mRNA vaccine; mRNA-1010) and mCOFLU ® (Combined Influenza and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine; mRNA-1083) for adults 50 years of age and older. Canada is the first country in the world to authorize both Moderna’s seasonal mRNA influenza vaccine and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine. “Health Canada’s authorizations of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU today mark another important step in bringing the benefits of mRNA technology to seasonal respiratory vaccination. It’s not every day that a company gets two product approvals on the same day,” said Stéphane Bancel, Chief Executive Officer of Moderna. “Influenza and COVID-19 continue to place a significant burden on public health, particularly among older adults. These milestones reflect our commitment to advancing innovative vaccine options that help protect Canadians and support more resilient health systems.” mFLUSIVA is Canada’s first mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, while mCOFLU is the country’s first combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine. Health Canada’s authorizations follow the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s approval of mFLUSIVA in August 2026 and the European Commission’s authorization of the Company’s combination influenza and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, marketed as mCOMBRIAX®, in April 2026. Both vaccines remain under regulatory review in additional markets. mFLUSIVA is authorized for active immunization of adults 50 years of age and older for the prevention of influenza disease caused by influenza virus subtypes A and B represented in the vaccine. i mCOFLU is authorized for active immunization of adults 50 years of age and older for the prevention of influenza disease caused by influenza virus types A and B represented in the vaccine and SARS-CoV-2. ii Health Canada’s authorization of mFLUSIVA is supported by the pivotal Phase 3 mRNA-1010-P304 study (NCT06602024), a randomized, active-controlled trial involving approximately 40,800 adults 50 years of age and older across 11 countries. mFLUSIVA met all pre-specified statistical success criteria, including the highest level of pre-specified superiority, demonstrating relative vaccine efficacy of 26.6% (95% CI: 16.7-35.4) in adults 50 years of age and older and 27.4% (95% CI: 12.1-40.0) in adults 65 years of age and older compared with a standard-dose inactivated influenza vaccine against RT-PCR-confirmed, protocol-defined influenza-like illness caused by influenza A or B. iii The authorization is also supported by the Phase 3 mRNA-1010-P303 Part C study (NCT05827978), which demonstrated superior antibody responses compared with a high-dose inactivated influenza vaccine in adults 65 years of age and older. iv Across both studies, the most commonly reported adverse reactions included injection-site pain, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, joint pain, chills and axillary (underarm) swelling or tenderness. Most solicited reactions were mild to moderate and resolved within one to two days. v mCOFLU builds on the clinical development of mFLUSIVA and mNEXSPIKE ® . Health Canada’s authorization of mCOFLU is supported by a pivotal Phase 3 trial (NCT06097273), a randomized, observer-blind, active-controlled study evaluating safety, reactogenicity and immunogenicity in two cohorts of approximately 4,000 adults each. Adults 65 years of age and older received mCOFLU or co-administered Fluzone HD ® , a high-dose influenza vaccine, and Spikevax ® , Moderna’s licensed COVID-19 vaccine. Adults 50 to 64 years of age received mCOFLU or co-administered Fluarix ® , a standard-dose influenza vaccine, and Spikevax. vi The study met all primary endpoints demonstrating non-inferiority of immune responses. Following a single dose, mCOFLU elicited statistically significantly higher immune responses against three influenza strains (A/H1N1, A/H3N2 and B/Victoria) and SARS-CoV-2 in both age cohorts compared with co-administered licensed comparator vaccines. The exception was B/Yamagata, a strain no longer recommended for inclusion in seasonal influenza vaccines, for which a statistically significantly higher immune response was not observed in adults 65 years of age and older. vii mCOFLU demonstrated an acceptable safety and tolerability profile. The most commonly reported adverse reactions included injection-site pain, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, joint pain, chills and axillary (underarm) swelling or tenderness. Most were mild to moderate and short in duration. No serious adverse events were assessed as related to mCOFLU in the pivotal study. viii Moderna will engage with Canadian health authorities and immunization partners as it advances plans for the future availability of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU in Canada. About Moderna Moderna is a pioneer and leader in the field of mRNA medicine. Through the advancement of its technology platform, Moderna is reimagining how medicines are made to transform how we treat and prevent diseases. Since its founding, Moderna’s mRNA platform has enabled the development of vaccines and therapeutics across infectious diseases, cancer, rare diseases and more. With a global team and a unique culture, driven by the company’s values and mindsets, Moderna’s mission is to deliver the greatest possible impact to people through mRNA medicines. A ‘Draw, Write and Tell’ Exploration of Children's Postpandemic Understanding of COVID-19 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月08日 来源:Child: Care, Health and Development 2 编辑推荐: 目的:本研究旨在采用“绘画-书写-讲述”(Draw, Write and Tell, DWT)方法探索后疫情时代儿童对COVID-19的认知。研究基于常识模型(Common Sense Model, CSM)的特征评估儿童绘画的准确性,考察其发展趋势,并探索儿 欢迎领取“抗体偶联药物前沿研发方案” 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 RESEARCH ARTICLE Open Access 目的:本研究旨在采用“绘画-书写-讲述”(Draw, Write and Tell, DWT)方法探索后疫情时代儿童对COVID-19的认知。研究基于常识模型(Common Sense Model, CSM)的特征评估儿童绘画的准确性,考察其发展趋势,并探索儿童在绘画中赋予COVID-19的视觉表征。设计:采用横断面参与式设计,在个体数据收集环节中运用DWT方法。方法:70名5–11岁儿童通过绘画和文字创作描绘COVID-19的图画,随后向研究人员描述其作品。数据在学校中个别收集。完整的视觉制品由儿童原始绘画、附带文字及研究人员标注组成。采用内容分析与反思性主题分析的双重方法对制品进行分析。结果:年长儿童对COVID-19的表征显著更为准确。准确性在CSM衍生的身份(Identity)、严重性(Severity)和病因(Cause)维度上最高,而对时间线(Timeline)、可治愈性(Curability)和治疗(Treatment)的理解在所有年龄组中均持续偏低。围绕儿童对COVID-19的认知构建了两个主题:COVID-19作为一种疾病和COVID-19作为一种生物实体。值得注意的是,所有年龄段的儿童均将COVID-19拟人化,年长儿童更倾向于如此。最后,儿童讨论了其COVID-19信息来源。结论:儿童对COVID-19的认知具有多面性,既涵盖疾病概念,也包括其生物学病因。这在后疫情时代对于设计和传播适合儿童发展阶段的健康信息宣传活动及小学阶段的生物学教育具有更广泛的启示。 **研究背景与问题** 欢迎领取《抗体药研发解决方案》领 取 自2020年疫情暴发以来,COVID-19作为一种隐性且复杂的威胁,深刻扰乱了日常生活的各个方面。由于这场前所未有的公共卫生紧急事件,健康信息宣传活动无处不在,但这些信息主要由成人设计并面向成人传播(Bray, Blake, et al. 2021; Christidou et al. 2021; Rowland and Cook 2021; Thompson et al. 2021)。儿童因此成为关于SARS-CoV-2及其传播风险和预防措施信息的间接接收者。一项大规模报告(G?tz et al. 2020)指出了这一差异的影响,结论认为儿童在掌握部分COVID-19知识的同时感到担忧,并能从更适合其年龄的信息中受益。自2023年5月起(World Health Organisation [WHO] 2023),COVID-19不再构成国际关注的突发公共卫生事件(Public Health Emergency of International Concern, PHEIC)。然而,这一背景为理解儿童如何概念化新发传染病提供了独特情境。探索儿童对COVID-19的视觉表征,作为使其隐性概念化变得可见的途径,可为未来面向儿童的健康信息传播提供关键框架。以往关于儿童健康威胁认知的发展趋势因疾病类型而异。儿童对AIDS的理解比流感更为详细,这归因于AIDS流行期间的信息暴露(Sigelman 2022)。其他疾病如水痘或麻疹相对被较好理解,各年龄段儿童均表现出对预防和康复的知识(Bir and Podmore 1990)。探索儿童对COVID-19认知的文献较为稀少。Thompson et al.(2021)发现儿童对COVID-19的理解涵盖三个主题:COVID-19作为一种传染性疾病、围绕疫情的负面情绪和社会责任。后者为疾病构念提供了一个有趣的组成部分,因为它在其他疾病的认知中并未出现。Labotka and Gelman(2023)报告称儿童对COVID-19和普通感冒的理解基本相似;然而当存在差异时,儿童对COVID-19的概念化准确性高于普通感冒。关键在于,上述数据均收集于疫情期间,当时关于COVID-19的信息无处不在。疫情之后儿童对COVID-19认知的这种高准确性是否得以保持,仍属未知。本研究采用Leventhal et al.(1980, 1992, 2016)的常识模型(CSM)作为组织儿童疾病感知细微差异的适当框架,该模型由五个核心维度组成:身份(Identity)、病因(Cause)、时间线(Timeline)、后果(Consequences)和控制(Control)。尽管该框架最初针对成人设计,但已有效用于组织儿童对不同疾病状况和以往流行病(如流感、普通感冒、AIDS和H1N1流感)的表征(e.g., Karademas et al. 2013; Law et al. 2014; Myant and Williams 2005; Williams et al. 2012; Wong and Sam 2011)。在CSM框架内已观察到发展趋势,年长儿童在病因、时间线、可治愈性和后果维度上表现出更好的理解(Fox et al. 2008; Wickering et al. 2023)。将CSM作为COVID-19研究框架的工作相对较少(e.g., Hayes et al. 2022; M?ller et al. 2022),且尚未有研究将CSM应用于儿童对COVID-19的认知。绘画此前已被用作阐明儿童和成人CSM维度的有效工具(Broadbent et al. 2019)。“绘画-书写-讲述”(DWT)是一种多功能的创造性研究方法,要求参与者根据提示提供绘画、包含标注并向研究人员描述其创作(Angell et al. 2015)。长期以来,它被认为是探索儿童健康和疾病认知的有用工具(e.g., Bradding and Horstman 1999; Liamputtong and Fernandes 2015; Pope et al. 2019; Xie et al. 2022),且不依赖复杂的语言技能(McWhirter 2014)。尽管儿童绘画能够有效探索其对COVID-19的认知(e.g., Bonoti et al. 2022; Christidou et al. 2021),但DWT尚未应用于此背景。年幼儿童在绘制微生物时倾向于使用拟人化,这一趋势随年龄增长和对生物学理解的深化而减弱(Byrne 2011)。有趣的是,Labotka and Gelman(2023)在探索儿童对COVID-19的认知时发现这一趋势发生了逆转,年长儿童比年幼儿童更多地将微生物拟人化。因此,DWT方法在深入捕捉儿童对COVID-19的认知方面具有独特优势。本研究是一个更大的多方法项目的一部分,该项目包括访谈和创造性方法,旨在考察儿童对COVID-19认知的发展变化。本文呈现的研究采用DWT方法探索后疫情时代儿童对COVID-19的认知,旨在:(1)基于CSM维度评估儿童绘画中所表征知识的准确性;(2)考察数据中的发展趋势;(3)探索儿童在绘画中赋予COVID-19的视觉表征:疾病、公共卫生信息和微生物。 **关键技术方法** 本研究采用横断面参与式设计,运用DWT方法进行个体数据收集。样本为70名5–11岁儿童(M = 8.5, SD = 2.1),均就读于英国苏格兰同一所国家资助小学,该区域属于苏格兰最不贫困的20%地区。数据收集于2023年11月至12月间共15天内在学校正常上课时间进行。每名儿童单独参与,被要求“你想让我看看COVID-19长什么样吗?你可以用绘画和文字”。完整的视觉制品包括儿童原始绘画、附带文字及研究人员标注。分析采用内容分析(基于CSM的九维度编码方案,评分0–3)和反思性主题分析的双重方法。定量数据使用R进行分析,采用非参数Wilcoxon秩和检验比较年幼组(5–7岁)和年长组(8–11岁)的准确性差异。 **研究结果** **内容分析**:年长儿童在CSM框架内对COVID-19的总体准确性中位数(0.44)显著高于年幼儿童(0.11)(W = 202.5, p < 0.001)。个体维度分析显示,身份(W = 360, p < 0.05)、严重性(W = 462, p < 0.05)和病因(W = 235, p < 0.001)维度的准确性在年长儿童中显著更高。然而,症状、预防、症状出现时间线、可治愈性、治疗和康复时间线在各年龄段均持续偏低,无显著变化。 **反思性主题分析**:构建了两个主题。主题1——COVID-19作为一种疾病,包含四个子主题:(1)感染COVID-19:涵盖传播机制和预防方法,儿童描绘了唾液、鼻、眼、手和污物等传播机制以及洗手、戴口罩和咳嗽时掩口等预防策略,但未将疫苗接种作为预防策略加以描绘;(2)患有COVID-19:涵盖生理、心理和社会方面,包括症状描述、情绪表达(最常见为悲伤,其次为愤怒和孤独)以及自我隔离或他人照护等社会层面;(3)COVID-19干预措施:包括状况评估(体温计、快速侧流抗原检测、PCR检测)和治疗(通用药物、居家 remedies、卧床休息),年长儿童更多提及状况评估而年幼儿童主要提及治疗;(4)COVID-19结局:呈现完全康复或死亡的二元结局,儿童多用文字描述而非绘画细节。主题2——COVID-19作为一种生物实体,包含六个子主题:(1)拟人化微生物:儿童赋予微生物人类特征、情感、社会动态和道德属性,年长儿童更倾向于描绘不道德行为;(2)微生物颜色:儿童使用颜色作为信息标记而非情感表达,最常见色调为绿色、红色和灰色,色相和饱和度均承载信息;(3)刺突功能:儿童对刺突功能提供了精细解释,包括维持结构完整性、防御其他细胞、感染机制、导航、移动和吸附等,该子主题平均年龄最高(11岁);(4)感染过程:儿童将感染过程呈现为病毒在体内增殖或接管健康细胞,并提及免疫系统的作用;(5)微生物数量:儿童绘制单个或多个微生物,绘制单个微生物的儿童年龄略大;(6)信息来源:儿童主要引用图像和视频作为信息来源,年长儿童更多引用视频,无儿童提及父母或教师作为直接信息来源。 **讨论与结论** 本研究采用DWT方法探索后疫情时代小学生对COVID-19的认知。通过内容分析和反思性主题分析的双重方法,揭示了儿童COVID-19概念的多面性和复杂性。内容分析作为演绎方法,表明儿童对COVID-19的认知存在明显的发展进程,年长儿童总体准确性更高,尤其在身份、严重性和病因维度;而时间线、可治愈性和治疗维度在各年龄段均持续偏低,这种不对称性提示某些方面可能更具发展敏感性,凸显了教育干预的重点领域。反思性主题分析作为归纳方法,深化了对儿童视觉表征的洞察。COVID-19被描绘为兼具生物学、心理学和社会表征的复杂概念。儿童对病毒刺突功能的归因是此前文献未讨论的独特发现,揭示了儿童构建科学意义的方式,表明其存在朴素生物学(na?ve biology)(Hatano and Inagaki 1994)。与传统的Piagetian视角不同,所有年龄段儿童均将COVID-19拟人化,年长儿童更倾向如此,这与Labotka and Gelman(2023)的发现一致。拟人化以不同方式出现,包括感知性拟人化,支持Airenti(2018)关于拟人化是基本人类态度而非儿童特有的论点。儿童还赋予病毒情感状态和道德倾向,这可能归因于英国公共卫生信息中的道德基调以及效果性动机(effectance motivation)以创造控制感(Waytz et al. 2010)。疾病相关情绪有所呈现,但明显缺乏恐惧和积极情绪,这可能归因于疫情已过去的时间。儿童未提及父母或教师作为信息来源,而是提及新闻或图像,这与Bray, Carter, et al.(2021)疫情期间国际研究形成鲜明对比,提示儿童健康信息获取在后疫情时代可能发生了转变。研究结论:本研究表明白小学生将COVID-19理解为多面性概念。儿童绘画中识别出明确的发展趋势,年长儿童在CSM的身份、严重性和病因维度上概念化准确性更高。无论年龄,时间线和可治愈性维度均存在知识差距,表明CSM各维度被不均衡地理解。此外,儿童绘画清晰展现了其对COVID-19的认知超越CSM维度,COVID-19既涵盖疾病概念也包括其生物实体,涉及拟人化、道德、朴素生物学和社会责任。这些结果在后疫情时代对设计和传播适合儿童发展阶段的健康信息宣传活动及小学阶段生物学教育具有更广泛的启示。 supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Sunday, November 8, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Machine Learning and Topological Analysis Identify COVID-19 in Lung Scans by November 8, 2026 in Health, Technology Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Machine Learning and Topological Analysis Identify COVID-19 in Lung Scans Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A mathematical imaging framework combining topological data analysis with supervised machine learning algorithms has achieved an accuracy rate of 97.5 percent and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve exceeding 0.99 in detecting COVID-19 from axial chest computed tomography scans. In an experimental evaluation reported by researchers Rabih Assaf, Abbas Rammal, Alban Goupil, Mohammad Kacim, and Valeriu Vrabie, persistent homology was applied to extract multi-scale structural descriptors of lung parenchyma, which were subsequently supplied to various automated classification architectures. The resulting experimental outcomes established that a Random Forest classifier attained a peak classification accuracy of 97.51 percent at a thirty percent testing split, while a Support Vector Machine utilizing a radial basis function kernel achieved the highest overall area under the curve value of 0.992495. By systematically capturing intrinsic geometric and homological structures within chest scans rather than depending exclusively on raw pixel intensity matrices or traditional localized pixel statistics, this analytical configuration demonstrates an automated diagnostic methodology capable of identifying viral pulmonary alterations across complex radiological datasets. The clinical motivation outlined in the investigation centers on the persistent vulnerabilities of established pathogenic diagnostic procedures alongside the operational challenges posed by global viral dissemination. While pathogenic laboratory examinations such as reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction testing remain the prevailing diagnostic standard for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, they carry notable operational limitations including processing turnaround delays and documented frequencies of false-negative outcomes. Conventional molecular tests identify viral genetic sequences directly from respiratory specimens, whereas rapid antigen screenings identify viral surface proteins at lower sensitivity, and serological examinations identify host antibody production but cannot diagnose acute phase illnesses. Consequently, chest radiography and computed tomography imaging modalities serve as vital adjunctive diagnostic pathways capable of highlighting pulmonary damage patterns, including ground-glass opacities, lung consolidations, and fine reticular anomalies that perturb the anatomical architecture of healthy lung tissue. To resolve these radiological challenges rapidly without overwhelming clinical facilities, the researchers formulated an automated computational pipeline designed to process high-dimensional radiological data, discern infection-induced structural alterations, and provide consistent classification without relying on subjective human observation. To capture high-dimensional geometric arrangements that evade classical statistical distributions, the proposed technique introduces concepts grounded in algebraic topology through topological data analysis. Unlike traditional geometrical models that simplify shapes into rudimentary cell complexes and lose fine quantitative information, topological data analysis extracts coarse-scale, global, and nonlinear structural invariants from spatial datasets. In this radiological implementation, two-dimensional grayscale lung slice images are formally converted into topological cubical complexes, designated as pixels complexes, wherein individual image pixels function as zero-dimensional vertices or zero-cells. Spatial connections between horizontally or vertically adjacent pixels differing by a single spatial unit coordinate are mapped as unit-length edges or one-cells, and the bounded regions enclosed by four perimeter edges are defined as unit squares or two-cells. This formal construction yields an integrated algebraic structure that simultaneously encapsulates discrete numerical pixel intensities alongside their exact spatial neighborhoods, generating a rigorous geometric baseline from which multi-scale topological features can be consistently measured across diverse radiological densities. Discover more Engineering job board Research publication platform Scientific instrument sales Laboratory equipment supplier Biotech startup funding Within the algebraic structure of the constructed pixels complex, formal linear combinations of k-cells are organized into k-chains with coefficients belonging to the binary finite field of integers modulo two. The aggregate set of these k-chains constitutes a sequence of chain groups interconnected by boundary operators that map k-dimensional chains directly into boundary chains of dimension k minus one. The mathematical integrity of this system relies on the fundamental topological condition establishing that the composition of successive boundary operators yields zero for every dimension, meaning that the boundary of a boundary is identically empty. Elements whose boundaries evaluate to zero constitute the k-th cycle subgroup, representing closed loops or voids that encircle spatial cavities without enclosing solid matter. Concurrently, elements formed by taking the boundary of higher-dimensional chains constitute the k-th boundary subgroup. Because the boundary subgroup forms a proper subset of the cycle subgroup, algebraic quotient groups designated as homology groups are formed by factoring cycle groups by their boundary groups. These quotient groups isolate persistent structural cavities, such as zero-dimensional connected components and one-dimensional enclosing loops, while mathematically discarding trivial boundaries. Because single static evaluations of homology groups fail to capture the evolutionary trajectory of spatial features across brightness gradients, the researchers instituted an intensity-driven filtration scheme to compute persistent homology. Under this ordering protocol, zero-cells inherit values directly corresponding to image pixel intensities, whereas each higher-dimensional k-cell is systematically assigned the maximum intensity exhibited among the lower-dimensional cells forming its immediate boundary. As a numerical threshold parameter advances monotonically, a nested sequence of expanding subcomplexes emerges, spanning from the empty set through the entire image complex. Throughout this sequential expansion, topological cavities emerge at specific birth thresholds and eventually terminate or merge into higher-dimensional structures at subsequent death thresholds. The lifespan of any topological class is computed as the quantitative difference between its destruction level and creation level, with prolonged lifespans designating stable, prominent structural properties of pulmonary tissue and brief lifespans representing radiological image noise. These multidimensional birth and death coordinates are summarized through persistence diagrams and persistence barcodes, calculated programmatically utilizing the Persistent Homology Algorithm Toolbox. From the persistent homology computations and standard image properties, the investigators engineered a compact vector comprising eight numerical features extracted from each processed lung computed tomography image. These eight quantitative descriptors encompass the mean lifespan and standard deviation of zero-dimensional homology cycles, the mean lifespan and standard deviation of one-dimensional homology cycles, the zero-dimensional persistent entropy, the one-dimensional persistent entropy, alongside the overall mean and standard deviation of image pixel intensities. Persistent entropy quantifies the structural diversity of the topological landscape by evaluating the normalized ratio of individual cycle lifespans against the aggregate sum of all lifespans through a logarithmic entropy formulation. These computed descriptors were then provided to five supervised machine learning models: Decision Trees as a logic-based classifier requiring no prior distributional assumptions, Random Forest as an ensemble tree model, Support Vector Machines utilizing a radial basis function kernel, Gaussian Naive Bayes reflecting conditional predictor probabilities, and Logistic Regression representing linear statistical modeling. The experimental dataset comprised eight hundred axial chest computed tomography scans collected in equal balance, consisting of four hundred images from confirmed COVID-19 patients and four hundred scans from healthy individuals without viral abnormalities. To eliminate radiological confounders and extraneous non-pulmonary anatomical structures, the team deployed an image preprocessing sequence beginning with spatial resizing that standardized all heterogeneous scans to dimensions of 128 by 128 pixels. The images were subsequently converted to a 256-level grayscale colormap and normalized to floating-point numerical values within a zero-to-one range. To amplify radiological contrast between the lung parenchyma and surrounding thoracic elements such as ribs, soft tissues, blood vessels, and cardiac structures, gamma correction contrast enhancement was implemented using a gamma parameter value of three, notably omitting artificial noise-reduction filters. Lung segmentation was subsequently performed by executing binary and triangle thresholding for normal scans alongside Otsu thresholding for COVID-19 scans, followed by mask generation to eliminate out-lung artifacts while retaining purely pulmonary parenchymal regions. Model training and evaluation were carried out using varying train-test dataset splits alongside k-fold cross-validation frameworks to verify predictive stability across unseen samples. The cross-validation protocol partitioned the processed imagery across multiple fold configurations including three, four, five, and ten folds, iteratively utilizing each partitioned subset for validation while remaining subsets served for model fitting. In baseline single-split evaluations, the Decision Tree classifier recorded an overall accuracy of 93.75 percent, an F1 score of 0.94, and an area under the curve of 0.93812 at a twenty percent testing split, demonstrating mean cross-validation accuracy of 91.72 percent with a standard deviation of 1.31 percent. The Logistic Regression model achieved a peak accuracy of 85.42 percent at a thirty percent testing split with an average area under the curve of 0.945505 and a cross-validation mean accuracy of 83.86 percent with a standard deviation of 1.03 percent. The Naive Bayes classifier demonstrated lower relative efficacy, recording an average accuracy of 84.09 percent, an F1 score of 0.8559, an area under the curve of 0.948845, and a cross-validation mean accuracy of 84.11 percent with a standard deviation of 1.64 percent across fold evaluations. The Random Forest and Support Vector Machine models demonstrated the highest performance across all quantitative evaluation metrics. The Random Forest classifier attained an accuracy of 97.51 percent at a thirty percent testing split, sustaining an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve above 0.99 across all testing sizes, alongside a cross-validation accuracy mean of 96.34 percent and a standard deviation of 0.72 percent across folds. The Support Vector Machine recorded a peak accuracy of 96.25 percent at a thirty percent testing split and established the highest area under the curve value among all models at 0.992495, maintaining a cross-validation accuracy mean of 94.51 percent with a standard deviation of 0.95 percent. The investigators noted that the Random Forest architecture derived stability from averaging decision trees to curtail prediction variance, while the Support Vector Machine benefited from mapping the linear algebraic formulations of homological features into higher-dimensional kernel space, distinctly separating pathological patterns from normal parenchymal variations. To rigorously verify the diagnostic necessity of the topological features, the authors executed ablation trials comparing performance when removing either topological or statistical descriptors from the models. When the identical classifiers were trained using solely the two basic pixel statistics of mean and standard deviation, maximum accuracy dropped to 94.7 percent and area under the curve reached 0.97328. Conversely, training on the six persistent homology features alone without pixel statistics yielded a maximum accuracy of 85.4 percent and an area under the curve of 0.86519, confirming that combining homological descriptors with statistical metrics achieves optimal predictive capability. External validation on a separate independent computed tomography dataset corroborated this performance, with the Support Vector Machine reaching 94.5 percent accuracy with an area under the curve of 0.93 and the Random Forest reaching 93.8 percent accuracy with an area under the curve of 0.94. Benchmarking against convolutional neural networks with three and four layers coupled to the classifiers demonstrated comparable peak accuracies between 92.3 and 95.7 percent, while remaining computationally distinct. The authors explicitly emphasize several operational limitations, noting that clinical variability in image quality, scanner equipment, motion artifacts, and low slice resolution could degrade classification performance in actual medical deployments, while persistent homology values lack the intuitive visual interpretability of traditional clinical biomarkers, necessitating expanded validation across diverse thoracic imaging formats and patient prognostic trajectories before clinical implementation. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Sunday, November 8, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Chemistry Computational Study Analyzes Plant Compounds Against SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease Target by November 7, 2026 in Chemistry Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Computational Study Analyzes Plant Compounds Against SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease Target Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A computational docking investigation evaluating nine phytochemicals from two medicinal plants associated with traditional Siddha formulations found that structurally diverse natural molecules can engage the catalytic and substrate-recognition regions of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease through distinct polar and hydrophobic mechanisms. The study, conducted by researchers Anbarasan K. and C. Sasikala, applied a standardized in silico docking protocol to compare how alkaloid, flavonoid, polyphenol, sterol, and triterpenoid scaffolds interact with the enzyme known as 3CLpro or Mpro. Across the tested panel, predicted binding free energies ranged from −6.43 kcal/mol to −11.43 kcal/mol, with the glycosylated flavonoid Rutin and the sterols Stigmasterol and β-Sitosterol exhibiting the most favorable predicted computational affinity scores. The target of the investigation, the SARS-CoV-2 main protease, is an essential viral enzyme responsible for cleaving large polyproteins into functional non-structural proteins required for viral replication and transcription machinery, including enzymes for RNA synthesis. Because the main protease is indispensable for viral maturation and features a conserved catalytic center based on the His41 and Cys145 dyad, it represents a primary focal point for antiviral inhibitor discovery. Additionally, scientific literature notes that the protease modulates host-cell pathways linked to innate immune defence and programmed cell death, and its activity has been suggested to play a role in systemic inflammatory manifestations observed during severe infection. Consequently, identifying small molecules capable of obstructing its active site remains an active avenue in antiviral development. Natural products and traditional healthcare systems, including India’s Siddha medicine, provide extensive reservoirs of structurally diverse secondary metabolites. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Siddha-based interventions gained public and clinical attention, particularly in Tamil Nadu where select traditional treatments were introduced into designated care facilities. Among these preparations is Sivanethirachooranam, a formulation classified under Gunapadam Mooligai that utilizes the seed of Elaeocarpus sphaericus, locally known as Rudraksha, which is purified, finely powdered, and traditionally combined with honey to manage conditions categorized in Siddha practice as sannipatha thodam, vikkal, pitta-associated dizziness, and specific kapha-related disorders. However, because clinical validation for many traditional botanical formulations is frequently constrained by heterogeneous trial designs and small cohorts, computational molecular modeling provides a preliminary screening method to assess whether individual constituents exhibit direct mechanistic affinity for viral targets. Discover more Study Chemistry chemical constituents Identify Plants Study Biology Get Rapid Tests To establish a controlled comparative framework, the researchers selected nine phytochemicals representing two plant sources: Elaeocarpus sphaericus and Aristolochia indica. Four compounds—Elaeocarpine, Grandisines, Quercetin, and Ellagic acid—were derived from reported phytochemical literature on E. sphaericus, providing alkaloidal and polyphenolic frameworks. The remaining five compounds—β-Sitosterol, Stigmasterol, Friedelin, Cycloeucalenol, and Rutin—were selected based on the documented chemical constituents of A. indica, supplying sterol, triterpenoid, and complex flavonoid glycoside scaffolds. Because earlier literature had already documented individual computational assessments for several of these molecules, the explicit purpose of this investigation was not to assert first-time discovery of binding activity, but to systematically analyze how scaffold rigidity, molecular weight, hydrogen-bonding capacity, and hydrophobic surface area alter binding geometry under identical AutoDock conditions. Before docking simulations commenced, two-dimensional structures were built using ChemDraw Professional version 12.0 and converted to three-dimensional conformations, followed by geometry optimization and energy minimization via the Merck Molecular Force Field 94 to eliminate unfavorable steric strain. Physicochemical characterization revealed notable structural variation across the ligand set, with molecular weights spanning from 257.33 g/mol for Elaeocarpine to 610.5 g/mol for Rutin. Grandisines, Quercetin, and Ellagic acid exhibited intermediate molecular masses of 276.37 g/mol, 302.23 g/mol, and 302.194 g/mol, respectively. In contrast, the sterol and triterpenoid derivatives displayed higher molecular weights, with Stigmasterol at 412.7 g/mol, β-Sitosterol at 414.7 g/mol, and both Friedelin and Cycloeucalenol at 426.7 g/mol. Conformational flexibility also diverged sharply: Elaeocarpine, Grandisines, Ellagic acid, and Friedelin presented zero rotatable bonds, reflecting rigid structures, whereas Stigmasterol and Cycloeucalenol possessed five rotatable bonds, and β-Sitosterol and Rutin each contained six. Discover more Find Lung Care Read Med Journals Check Symptoms The structural model chosen for the viral target was the experimentally determined crystal structure of SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro complexed with inhibitor N3, retrieved from the RCSB Protein Data Bank under accession code PDB ID: 6LU7, solved at an X-ray crystallographic resolution of 2.16 Å with an R value of approximately 0.202. Using AutoDock Tools, water molecules and the co-crystallized N3 ligand were stripped, polar hydrogen atoms were added, Kollman united-atom charges were applied, and solvation parameters were established. Validation through the MolProbity server confirmed high stereochemical quality, placing 97.05% of protein residues within favored regions of the Ramachandran plot with zero residues in disallowed regions, alongside an overall Ramachandran Z-score of −1.92 ± 0.41 and 87.17% of side-chain rotamers residing in favored conformations. The docking grid was constructed with AutoGrid, centered at coordinates x = −9.732 Å, y = 11.403 Å, and z = 68.925 Å with a 60 × 60 × 60 point grid box and 0.375 Å spacing, encompassing His41, Cys145, and the broader substrate-binding cleft. Simulations utilized the Lamarckian Genetic Algorithm coupled with Solis and Wets local searching across two independent runs per compound, capping energy evaluations at 250,000 per run with an initial population of 150 individuals, a translational step size of 0.2 Å, and rotational and torsional step sizes of 5°. When the resulting poses were ranked by calculated binding free energy, Rutin demonstrated the strongest predicted binding affinity at −11.43 kcal/mol, paired with a calculated inhibition constant of 4.19 nM, an electrostatic energy contribution of −0.03 kcal/mol, an intermolecular energy of −6.73 kcal/mol, and a total interaction surface of 840.57 Å2. In comparison, Stigmasterol achieved −9.66 kcal/mol with a calculated Ki of 82.60 mM, an intermolecular energy of −10.11 kcal/mol, and an interaction surface of 811.29 Å2, while β-Sitosterol scored −9.09 kcal/mol with a predicted Ki of 216.19 nM, an intermolecular energy of −10.37 kcal/mol, and the largest interaction surface area among all ligands at 946.79 Å2. The triterpenoids Friedelin and Cycloeucalenol produced docking free energies of −8.72 kcal/mol and −8.68 kcal/mol, accompanied by predicted inhibition constants of 406.72 nM and 318.21 nM, intermolecular energies of −8.72 kcal/mol and −10.60 kcal/mol, and surface contact areas of 866.97 Å2 and 946.67 Å2, respectively. Meanwhile, the smaller phenolic and alkaloidal molecules displayed moderate binding energies: Ellagic acid scored −7.04 kcal/mol with a Ki of 6.89 μM; Grandisines reached −6.89 kcal/mol with a Ki of 8.89 μM; Elaeocarpine yielded −6.86 kcal/mol with a Ki of 9.44 μM; and Quercetin showed −6.43 kcal/mol with a Ki of 19.38 μM. These smaller scaffolds generated comparatively compact total interaction surfaces, measuring 592.17 Å2 for Ellagic acid, 635.61 Å2 for Elaeocarpine, 642.93 Å2 for Quercetin, and 679.77 Å2 for Grandisines, alongside modest electrostatic contributions between −0.01 and −0.33 kcal/mol. Detailed examination of the simulated binding poses revealed distinct amino-acid engagement profiles across the catalytic site and neighboring substrate-recognition residues, which include Leu27, Gly143, His163, His164, Met165, Glu166, Pro168, and His172. Stigmasterol engaged the highest number of predefined core residues, forming seven contacts across Phe140, Asn142, Gly143, Cys145, His163, Met165, Glu166, Pro168, His172, Gln189, and Gln192, directly interacting with catalytic residue Cys145 although lacking contact with His41. Both β-Sitosterol and Grandisines engaged six core residues; β-Sitosterol contacted Leu27, His41, Met49, Asn142, Ser144, Cys145, Met165, Glu166, Pro168, and Gln189, whereas Grandisines contacted His41, Met49, Tyr54, Gly143, Cys145, His163, Met165, Glu166, and Gln189, allowing both compounds to contact both catalytic dyad partners simultaneously. Rutin, Cycloeucalenol, and Quercetin each established contacts with five core residues. Rutin engaged Thr25, Leu27, His41, Phe140, Asn142, Ser144, Cys145, His163, Met165, and Gln189, successfully spanning both His41 and Cys145 within the active site. Cycloeucalenol contacted Thr25, Leu27, His41, Met49, Asn142, Cys145, Met165, Pro168, and Gln192, also engaging both catalytic residues. Conversely, Quercetin contacted His41, Phe140, Asn142, His163, Met165, Glu166, His172, and Gln189, interacting with His41 while omitting contact with Cys145. For the remaining molecules, Elaeocarpine and Ellagic acid each engaged four core residues, with both ligands contacting both His41 and Cys145, while Friedelin established three core residue interactions encompassing Thr25, His41, Asn142, Cys145, Met165, and Gln189. The study highlights how distinct chemical architectures achieve affinity through complementary energetic mechanisms. In the comparison between Quercetin and its glycoside Rutin, the addition of a disaccharide moiety expands Rutin’s polar functionality to ten hydrogen-bond donors and sixteen acceptors, allowing extensive multipoint polar interactions that yield a substantially more negative docking score than Quercetin’s compact aglycone core. In sharp contrast, the sterols Stigmasterol and β-Sitosterol possess only one hydrogen-bond donor and one acceptor, relying instead on hydrophobic packing, van der Waals forces, and large non-polar contact surfaces to achieve favorable docking energetics within the protease cavity. The authors emphasize critical methodological limitations inherent to docking simulations. Computational docking scores and AutoDock-calculated inhibition constants represent static energetic estimates rather than direct measurements of biochemical enzyme inhibition or antiviral efficacy. Furthermore, high predicted target affinity does not account for pharmacokinetic hurdles; Rutin’s molecular weight and high hydrogen-bonding count exceed Lipinski Rule-of-Five thresholds, presenting challenges for oral bioavailability and membrane permeability. Because the investigation evaluated a rigid crystal receptor without dynamic simulation, the authors conclude that molecular dynamics trajectories, MM-PBSA or MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations, in vitro enzymatic inhibition assays, ADME profiling, and cell-based viral replication studies remain necessary to determine whether any of these prioritized botanical scaffolds possess genuine therapeutic utility. (Arkansas Democrat-Gazette/Stephen Swofford) Philander Smith University announced this week that it has shifted to virtual instruction “following a limited number of COVID-19 cases.” In-person classes are expected to resume next Monday, the historically Black university in Little Rock said in a social media post on Tuesday. Activities scheduled from Monday onward will proceed, the post says. Homecoming activities through Sunday are canceled except for an outdoor 5K on Saturday, which will occur with health precautions, the post says. Participants from the campus community will be asked to test, according to the post. supplementary_news.content: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia skip to main content skip to footer Search Expand Menu About Us Our People Education Banking Careers Calendar of Events The Economy Expand Sub-Topics Monetary Policy Banking & Financial Markets Macroeconomics Regional Economics Consumer Finance Expand Sub-Topics Payment Systems Consumer Credit Education Finance Mortgage Markets Community Development Expand Sub-Topics Inclusive Growth Credit & Capital Housing & Neighborhoods Workforce & Economic Development SURVEYS & DATA Expand Sub-Topics REAL-TIME DATA RESEARCH Regional Economic Analysis CONSUMER FINANCE DATA COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DATA Search Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia The Economy How Did the U.S. Policy Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic Affect Inflation and Economic Growth? Article How Did the U.S. Policy Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic Affect Inflation and Economic Growth? 03 Nov ’26 Research in Focus — Fiscal transfers during the pandemic averted a depression-scale collapse at the cost of higher inflation rates, but supply-side disruptions explain most of the inflation surge. Share U.S. inflation has recently spiked to levels not seen since the 1970s. Economists have sought to understand the causes of this unexpected surge, which followed the COVID-19 pandemic.1 The U.S. government’s immediate response to the economic collapse caused by the pandemic was a series of fiscal transfers in 2020–2021 that included the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act; the Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act; and the American Rescue Plan. These fiscal transfers together amounted to 11 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2019 dollars. What was the impact of these enormous transfer payments on the macroeconomy? For their paper “Are Fiscal Transfers Inflationary?” Jonas Arias and Minchul Shin of the Philadelphia Fed and Juan Rubio-Ramírez of Emory University and the Atlanta Fed (as well as a visiting scholar at the Philadelphia Fed) studied the evolution of the U.S. economy during the pandemic with a particular emphasis on the role played by fiscal transfers in determining the dynamics of inflation and output. Using a recently developed econometric framework, they examined how key macroeconomic indicators interacted with each other and responded to unexpected shocks over time, how effective fiscal transfers were and at what cost in terms of inflation, and the role that monetary policy played in shaping macroeconomic outcomes.2 The authors used an econometric model, technically known as a rotation-invariant time-varying structural vector autoregression, to quantify the main forces behind changes in the economy.3 In particular, their framework allowed them to disentangle the contributions to output growth and inflation from fiscal transfer shocks; from demand shocks (resulting from, for example, the economywide shutdown early in the pandemic); and from monetary policy shocks from unexpected policy rate adjustments, which affect borrowing costs. They also studied supply shocks — specifically, those stemming from global supply chain shortages — as well as cost-push-related supply shocks. They found that demand shocks initially had a negative impact on both output and the price level as private spending collapsed in 2020. Later, some positive demand shocks occurred from, for example, pent-up demand following the lockdown. This pent-up demand boosted output and reversed the downward pressure on the price level exerted by the spending collapse at the onset of the pandemic. But overall, these demand shocks were not meaningful contributors to inflation during the pandemic — although they did contribute to the rise in short-term interest rates during the recovery phase. Meanwhile, they found that monetary policy shocks overall caused prices to be lower than they otherwise would have been. (This is because the effective lower bound on interest rates left the monetary authorities little room to lower rates further to stimulate the economy.) Postpandemic fiscal transfer shocks, however, significantly lifted output and accounted for a sizable share of the inflation that occurred through mid-2021. These payments dramatically improved economic activity, but this effect was short-lived, with their contribution to GDP diminishing by the end of 2021. The transfers raised the GDP deflator (which measures the price level) by 5 percent in 2021 alone and continued to contribute significantly to the price level through the end of 2024. Even so, fiscal transfers were not the main driver of the price level surge. It was instead the supply shocks that occurred from 2021 onward, reflecting widespread global supply bottlenecks and disruptions in logistics, that contributed the most to inflation and also negatively affected output. To cite just one example, supply-side price pressures mounted because of the global semiconductor chip shortage, creating supply chain disruptions for many U.S. manufacturing industries. Cost-push supply shocks further contributed to inflation, including through product price markups. How did monetary policy influence macroeconomic conditions during the pandemic? Early in the pandemic, monetary policy was contractionary, as the effective lower bound prevented the Federal Reserve from reducing the federal funds rate below zero in the first half of 2020. This contractionary policy weighed on output and the price level. Thereafter, the monetary policy response was expansionary because, through the lens of the econometric framework, the Federal Reserve delayed raising interest rates. Even so, this delayed response was not enough to make monetary policy’s overall contribution to the price level positive during the pandemic era. To learn more about the role of monetary policy in shaping how the expansion of fiscal transfers propagated through the economy, the authors compared the monetary policy response to fiscal transfer shocks during the pandemic with the response during the Great Recession (2007–2009). During the Great Recession, fiscal transfers were about one-quarter of those during the pandemic, and output contracted sharply. Meanwhile, the monetary policy response was systematic and strong, preventing significant inflation, although at the cost of providing weaker support for output. In contrast, a more muted policy response occurred following the pandemic, amplifying the output effects of the transfers but failing to prevent the fiscal transfer shocks from fueling inflation. Using counterfactual analysis, the authors replaced the Great Recession’s fiscal shocks with the large transfers from the pandemic and found that prices would still have risen, but more modestly than during the pandemic. This is because interest rates would have increased much more during the Great Recession as a result of systematic monetary policy adjustments.4 Their findings underscore that monetary policy plays a critical role in how fiscal transfers impact the macroeconomy. They conclude that, despite the unwanted inflation, U.S. fiscal transfers during the pandemic were essential in preventing an output collapse similar to the one experienced during the Great Depression. Without these transfers, real GDP per capita would have fallen by over 20 percent, rivaling the decline during the early 1930s. The cost of these transfers has been a sizable increase in the price level through mid-2021 with diminishing but persistent positive contributions to the price level through the end of 2024. The views expressed here are solely those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia or the Federal Reserve System. See, for example, Olivier Blanchard and Ben Bernanke, “What Caused the U.S. Pandemic-Era Inflation?” National Bureau of Economic Research Working Paper 31417 (2023), https://doi.org/10.3386/w31417. They extended the methodology introduced in the paper they wrote with Daniel Waggoner, “Inference Based on Time-Varying SVARs Identified with Sign Restrictions,” Review of Economic Studies (forthcoming). Their framework contains six key variables: fiscal transfers relative to GDP; real output growth per capita; the GDP deflator; the one-year Treasury yield, which captures changes in the policy rate and adjustments to the Federal Reserve’s balance sheet; the Institute for Supply Management Manufacturing Supplier Deliveries Index, which captures delivery delays; and the personal savings rate, which reflects households’ marginal decisions between spending and saving in response to fiscal transfers. They emphasize that “identifying the causal effects of fiscal transfers requires separating exogenous policy innovations [that is, unplanned interventions] from systematic policy responses [that is, standard rule-like adjustments] to macroeconomic conditions.”

Southeast Asia 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月08日 来源:Pulmonary Therapy 3.4 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Original Research Open access 引言 长COVID(Long COVID)是一种异质性感染后状态,发生于急性严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)感染后。围绕其定义、疾病负担、诊断和管理的持续不确定性,使东南亚地区的临床识别和照护复杂化。方法 研究人员在来自六个东南亚国家的十二名专家中开展了一项改良Delphi(德尔菲)共识研究,以制定关于长COVID的区域性指导。共识预先定义为≥80%一致,即12名专家中至少10名在多项选择题中选择相同回答,或在Likert(李克特)量表问题上表示同意(例如同意/强烈同意,最重要/更重要,相关/高度相关)。达到共识的问题从后续轮次中删除,未解决问题则修订、合并或扩展。在最后一轮中,对未达到共识的Likert量表问题采用事后描述性类别“中等支持”,以五点重要性量表(“最重要”至“最不重要”)中的“重要”作为中点类别,以捕捉被认为重要但未达到共识阈值的回答。结果 所有“定义”“疾病负担”和“管理”主题问题以及大多数“诊断”问题均达到共识。专家将长COVID定义为SARS-CoV-2感染后持续>3个月且无法解释的症状,区别于急性COVID-19后状态(post-acute COVID-19),且无最低严重程度阈值要求。长COVID被认为影响约6%–10%的SARS-CoV-2感染后个体,与已发表的世界卫生组织(WHO)和韩国感染病学会(KSID)估计一致;建议通过临床评估和症状导向检测进行诊断。急性COVID-19期间住院被确定为发生长COVID的危险因素。专家建议多学科、症状导向照护、康复、活动节律管理(pacing)和随访。疫苗接种和再感染预防被支持作为重要的长COVID风险降低策略,并且对于高风险个体,应考虑早期抗病毒治疗以预防严重急性疾病和住院。对于诊断所需的既往病史未达到共识;对加强针状态、缺乏早期抗病毒治疗、COVID前健康评估和标准化患者报告结局工具观察到中等支持。结论 该Delphi研究为东南亚长COVID提供了实用的区域性共识框架。 研究背景:急性SARS-CoV-2感染后持续症状自2020年中受到关注,2020年ICD编码和2021年WHO临床病例定义发布后逐步获得正式认可。但主要卫生机构对长COVID(Long COVID,SARS-CoV-2感染后持续症状)的定义仍存在明显差异:WHO要求症状在感染后3个月内出现并持续至少2个月;英国国家卫生与临床优化研究所(NICE)区分“ongoing symptomatic COVID-19”(4–12周)与“post-COVID-19 syndrome”(超过12周);美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)和美国国家科学院、工程院和医学院(NASEM)将其定义为感染后至少3个月的慢性状态;KSID(韩国感染病学会)和马来西亚卫生部则描述为诊断后超过3个月无法解释的症状。上述定义未统一要求实验室确认,未规定最低症状严重度或功能受损阈值,持续时间亦不一致,影响临床识别、研究可比性和治疗规划。多数长COVID患病率数据来自高收入国家,而亚洲及东南亚支持系统可能存在缺口,区域识别不足且具体行动有限;已有Delphi共识未针对亚洲定制。因此,研究人员开展区域改良Delphi共识研究,以形成东南亚长COVID定义、疾病负担、诊断和管理建议,指导临床实践并为卫生政策提供依据。 领取义翘神州针对Omicron的一站式解决方案 领 取 10%已发表估计的认可,并非东南亚实测患病率;共识认为其影响所有年龄和社会经济背景,但35–65岁和低收入群体负担更重,约五分之一受影响者症状严重;长COVID对日常功能和经济生产力造成挑战,原文引用日本2024年720亿美元生产力损失及台湾120亿美元、相当于GDP 1.5%的损失;泰国337名既往感染者中32.9%发生长COVID,焦虑28.5%、疲劳26.1%、呼吸困难13.4%常见;越南1507名12–17岁儿童中5.6%符合WHO标准,记忆下降85.9%、注意力差58.8%、疲劳57.6%常见,并伴学业中断和缺勤增加;12/12(100%)认为需要证据化政策、临床与公众教育及专门资源。Theme 3:Diagnosis(诊断)。多数诊断问题达成共识。专家组认为长COVID可累及任何器官系统,疲劳、运动后不适、认知障碍和气短常见,文献记录相关症状超过200种;目前无验证性生物标志物,诊断主要依赖临床评估和患者病史,检查用于评估并发症和共病而非确认长COVID;专科长COVID门诊评估应包括急性感染史、工作/家庭/社会领域功能影响及症状变化监测,COVID前健康状态评估和标准化患者报告结局工具C19-YRSm(改良COVID-19约克郡康复量表)仅获中等支持(均由8/12、66.7%升至含中点12/12、100%);症状导向实验室检测和专科转诊用于排除替代诊断。风险分层方面,未及时更新COVID-19疫苗接种和急性COVID-19期间住院为发生长COVID的危险因素达成共识;其他危险因素包括既往慢性病、高体质指数(BMI)、严重急性COVID-19、感染时未接种疫苗和重复SARS-CoV-2感染。专家组未就诊断是否必须依据临床或需有SARS-CoV-2聚合酶链反应(PCR)/快速抗原检测(RAT)阳性记录达成共识;约30%感染可能无症状。缺乏早期抗病毒治疗(8/12,66.7%;含中点10/12,83.3%)和加强针逾期(4/12,33.3%;含中点10/12,83.3%)仅为中等支持。Theme 4:Management(管理)。管理主题达成共识:长COVID无单一获批药物治疗,需个体化、症状导向管理。症状治疗共识包括:持续呼吸困难可调整吸入剂剂量或采用疾病特异治疗;慢性感染后咳嗽可用抗组胺药和鼻内糖皮质激素;原发性头痛在排除继发原因后对症治疗;嗅觉障碍采用嗅觉训练联合局部糖皮质激素鼻喷剂;不明原因疲劳在排除其他原因后以康复治疗为一线;睡眠障碍应消除干扰因素并处理病因;焦虑或抑郁需精神科转诊以排除其他原因,严重精神症状或自伤风险应立即咨询。康复与随访方面,共识支持由单一临床医生进行规律长期随访、向患者解释诊断和预后、以症状导向的活动节律管理(pacing)优于常规渐进运动,并可考虑常规使用17项C19-YRS。预防方面,共识支持对有症状、非住院高风险急性COVID-19个体考虑早期使用获批抗病毒药以预防重症和住院;目前无抗病毒药被正式批准专门预防长COVID,但急性期5天内使用现有口服抗病毒药可能降低长COVID风险;共识支持按推荐接种COVID-19疫苗包括加强针,以及在拥挤室内环境佩戴合适口罩、手卫生、咳嗽礼仪和良好室内通风。 研究结论部分译文:该Delphi共识研究为改善东南亚长COVID照护提供了及时且可操作的框架,作为该地区的区域指导而非普适性指导。通过在定义、疾病负担、诊断和管理等核心领域达成一致,该研究有助于减少可能阻碍临床识别、研究可比性和患者照护的现有不一致。其结果对长COVID仍被低估且正式指导有限的地区尤其相关。研究结果还强调需要公平获得评估、康复和支持服务,尤其对脆弱人群。同时,未达成共识和中等支持的领域表明证据基础仍不完整,需要进一步研究以完善风险分层、诊断工具和专科门诊评估。 supplementary_news.content_title: Omicron a 'different foe' that needs new plan: Ardern
supplementary_news.content: Most who catch omicron will recover at home, thanks to high vaccination rates, says Ardern. (Image: Getty) Prime minister Jacinda Ardern begins the political new year in earnest with the announcement of the “new plan” required to combat the inevitable spread of the highly transmissible omicron variant of covid-19 through the New Zealand population. In opening remarks to the Labour party’s caucus retreat at a coastal resort south of New Plymouth, Ardern said omicron was a “different foe”. “Now we will experience cases in New Zealand at a level we haven’t experienced before.” However, most cases would recover at home because high vaccination rates would reduce the severity of illness for most who contracted the virus. They were her most explicit comments yet about the extent to which NZ’s previous approaches to covid – elimination and then suppression – will not work once omicron gets into the community. Two further cases of omicron have been confirmed in the community in Auckland overnight, with Auckland district health board documents leaked to Māori TV estimating that once omicron becomes established in NZ, total daily cases of around 50,000 can be expected over a 12-to-16 week outbreak. With Ardern and covid response minister Chris Hipkins already conceding omicron will become established, the prime minister said the latest variant represented a “different challenge” to previous variants. While NZ had suppressed the prevalence of the delta covid variant better than many other countries and was among the most highly vaccinated populations in the world, omicron was a “different foe” and there were likely to be more variants after omicron. She rallied her caucus troops saying she felt resolute and confident, particularly because the approach to delta had worked and given New Zealanders a summer holiday, while the rollout of boosters and vaccination for five-to-11 year-olds was putting NZ in a position that many other countries were not in. “This time last year, we were not vaccinated,” she said. Now, as well as vaccination, there were anti-viral drugs becoming available. Ardern is expected to announce any changes to the so-called ‘traffic light’ covid protection system this afternoon, with the only likely move being a possible reduction in the ‘red’ status of the Northland region falling to orange. However, of greater significance will be the detail of announcements that are expected to cover how the government will approach the almost inevitable omicron surge. Hipkins yesterday would not be drawn ahead of a cabinet discussion yesterday afternoon, but acknowledged the concern that there could be very high levels of workers off work during the outbreak, that it was a matter of judgement as to whether to let the virus peak fast or try to spread out its impact, and that the need for MIQ for arrivals from offshore could be greatly reduced once the virus was established here. Among considerations is the extent to which the timing of the outbreak can be ‘controlled’ to occur in late summer rather than drifting into winter, when it would coincide with the winter flu season and potentially put greater strain on the public health system.
